summary: datefmt-pro postinstall exfiltrates host reconnaissance to hardcoded remote IP
details: datefmt-pro@1.0.0 advertises itself as a date/timezone utility, but its postinstall.js lifecycle script runs `whoami`, `hostname`, `uname -a`, `pwd`, captures node/npm versions, and enumerates non-internal IPv4 interfaces via os.networkInterfaces(), then POSTs the collected host-identity JSON to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://129.204.76.212/rce-poc over plain HTTP. The script runs automatically on `npm install`. index.js provides only a trivial date-formatter surface and contains an internal comment acknowledging that the visible library is a decoy while the actual payload lives in postinstall.js. The declared package purpose does not require host reconnaissance or outbound network calls to a bare-IP endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
